ISSUE:
Trim sets incorrect duration
If Trim end is after EOF, stream output duration is greater than expected.

INSTRUCTIONS:

Remember, YOU CAN ONLY ENTER ONE COMMAND AT A TIME. You should always wait for feedback after every command.
When you're satisfied with all of the changes you've made, you can submit your changes to the code base by simply running the submit command.
Note however that you cannot use any interactive session commands (e.g. python, vim) in this environment, but you can write scripts and run them. E.g. you can write a python script and then run it with `python <script_name>.py`.

NOTE ABOUT THE EDIT COMMAND: Indentation really matters! When editing a file, make sure to insert appropriate indentation before each line!

1. Always start by trying to replicate the bug that the issues discusses.

If the bug reproduction script requires inputting/reading a specific file, such as buggy-input.png, and you'd like to understand how to input that file, conduct a search in the existing repo code, to see whether someone else has already done that. Do this by running the command: find_file "buggy-input.png" If that doesn't work, use the linux 'find' command.

The currently open file might be in a different directory than the working directory! Note that some commands, such as 'create', open files, so they might change the current  open file.

The purpose is coarse chunking for later categorization. Prefer a few large sections over many detailed sections.

Use natural boundaries such as headings, labeled sections, or clear changes in subject.

Possible examples include bug_fixing, validation, performance_optimization, documentation, configuration, feature_implementation, investigation, or refactoring. These examples are not exhaustive; use other established programming terms when they describe the conversation more accurately. Include only intents supported by the conversation. Do not include technologies, tools, files, or technical areas.

tool_call.prompt: Given this conversation, list the specific tools or commands invoked by tool calls. Identify the concrete operation instead of abstracting it into a broad category. Use concise lowercase snake_case names matching the invoked tool or command, such as grep, rg, find, ls, file, cat, sed, git, npm, bun, tsc, read_file, write_file, edit_file, or generate_image. These examples are not exhaustive; use the actual tool or command found in the conversation. For shell tool calls, inspect the command and classify by its primary executable rather than using generic names such as shell, command_execution, search_tool, file_operation, or version_control. Include not_tool_call for content that is not a tool call.
